data.title: PtdIns(3,4,5)P3-Dependent Activation of the mTORC2 Kinase Complex
data.authors: Liu P; Gan W; Chin YR; Ogura K; Guo J; Zhang J; Wang B; Blenis J; Cantley LC; Toker A; Su B; Wei W

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: PIP3 relieves SIN1 PH-domain autoinhibition to activate the mTORC2 kinase complex.
data.abstract_excerpt: mTOR serves as a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism by forming two distinct complexes, mTORC1 and mTORC2. Although mechanisms of mTORC1 activation by growth factors and amino acids have been extensively studied, the upstream regulatory mechanisms leading to mTORC2 activation remain largely elusive. Here, we report that the pleckstrin homology (PH) domain of SIN1, an essential and unique component of mTORC2, interacts with the mTOR kinase domain to suppress mTOR activity.

extracted_findings.effect: PIP3 binds the SIN1 PH domain to relieve suppression of mTOR → activates mTORC2
